My go-to transcription tool on Mac, MacWhisper, received another major update today, adding live meeting transcription, significantly improved speaker identification, deeper Apple Intelligence integration, and brand-new transcription models. Here's everything new.

MacWhisper integrates even deeper with Apple Intelligence

I've talked numerous times in the past about how much I rely on MacWhisper, especially in my workflow for producing podcasts.

MacWhisper was one of the very first AI transcription tools on Mac. Since independent developer Jordi Bruin launched it back in 2023, it has continued to improve and expand support for new models, services, and workflows.

These include automatic meeting recording and speaker identification, folder watching, system-wide dictation, local and cloud-based AI models, as well as integration with services like Notion, Zapier, Obsidian, and n8n.

Today, MacWhisper updates to version 15.2, adding improved speaker identification powered by NVIDIA's Nemotron 3 Diarization model, which was just announced a few hours ago.

Speaking of the other big feature in today's update: live meeting transcription.

This has been high on MacWhisper's public roadmap, and now it's finally here, allowing users to read, revisit, copy, or send live transcriptions in real time during meetings.

As for the actual transcription models, MacWhisper 15.2 adds Alibaba's QWEN3-ASR transcription model, which supports 22 languages, while also integrating more tightly with Apple Intelligence, Siri, Spotlight, and Shortcuts on macOS 27.

Users running macOS (including those in the EU) can now search transcriptions system-wide, open them with Siri, drag text into Shortcuts, and reference the transcription currently on screen in Siri or Apple Intelligence requests.

Finally, MacWhisper 15.2 adds folders and subfolders for organising transcriptions and meeting notes, as well as the ability to drag existing transcriptions into folders from the sidebar.
